gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Heavy, bold Plakkaat curls its terminals nearly back to the stem, a closed and tight look. But Noto Sans Zanabazar Square opens wide, with a soaring x-height that stays crisp even when it shrinks.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-traditional-: Noto Traditional Nushu reads like a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut, with bowls filling the line. Plakkaat's closed, bent-straw heading sits against it, and paragraphs flow along without tiring.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-numans: Plakkaat pours its heavy letters out like ink at a single width, with terminals sweeping round toward the stem. And Numans spreads out its coiled lowercase with generous tracking, doing the quiet work the heading leaves alone.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-onest: Onest has short ascenders above big bowls and a gentle monotone line, so it reads approachably and smoothly. Beside Plakkaat's closed heavy forms it keeps going comfortably, paragraph after paragraph.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-open-sans: Contemporary and smooth, Open Sans has bulky lowercase proportions and no clogged curves to snag the eye. And Plakkaat, outlined at one steady thickness and closed up tight, makes that openness feel even easier across a full page.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-orienta: Modern in outlook, Plakkaat draws its heavy letters with terminals that curl nearly shut. Orienta lets its counters breathe like a hollow reed cut open, so a long passage stays light and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-oxygen: Heavy and tightly curled, Plakkaat brings its terminals right round toward the stem in a bold display voice. Oxygen sits beneath with curves left open, and its lowercase nearly matches the capitals.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-parkinsans: Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness everywhere, with wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk and lowercase rising close to capitals. Plakkaat's closed, heavy forms take the loud part, leaving this plain sans the quiet one.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-pathway-extreme: Modern and tidy, Plakkaat has no hairlines anywhere, just heavy forms with terminals that curl nearly shut. Pathway Extreme counters with clear openings in its rounds and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height, which suits steady text.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-preahvihear: Plakkaat is a heavy display face with terminals that sweep round to nearly touch the stem, and a low contrast between capitals and body height. Preahvihear opens its letters like a pried oyster shell under a lofty x-height, so extended reading feels light.
